Spatiotemporal Models for Agricultural Experiments

bayesAgriFlow

Source: vignettes/v33-spatiotemporal-foundations.Rmd
v33-spatiotemporal-foundations.Rmd

Purpose

Version 1.2.0 adds an explicit space-time layer to bayesAgriFlow. The scientific goal is to distinguish spatial dependence, temporal persistence, fixed agronomic effects, and posterior prediction rather than treating repeated maps as independent snapshots (Cressie and Wikle 2011).

1. Scientific structure

A spatiotemporal agricultural dataset contains observations indexed simultaneously by location and time. Experimental treatment structure remains separate from the latent process.

d <- bayes_teaching_data("spatiotemporal")
des <- bayes_spatiotemporal(d, "yield", "x", "y", "day", ~ treatment, subject = "plot_id")
if (FALSE) bayes_st_monitor(des)

Interpretation checklist

  • Identify the experimental unit and the repeated series.
  • Keep treatment effects distinct from latent spatial and temporal structure.
  • Quantify uncertainty on the response scale.
  • Avoid treating a smooth posterior mean map as observed truth.
  • State when inference is interpolation versus extrapolation.

2. Design before fitting

Use bayes_spatiotemporal() to declare response, coordinates, time, series identifiers, fixed effects, and the spatial and temporal structures before any sampling begins.

d <- bayes_teaching_data("spatiotemporal")
des <- bayes_spatiotemporal(d, "yield", "x", "y", "day", ~ treatment, subject = "plot_id")
if (FALSE) bayes_st_monitor(des)

Interpretation checklist

  • Identify the experimental unit and the repeated series.
  • Keep treatment effects distinct from latent spatial and temporal structure.
  • Quantify uncertainty on the response scale.
  • Avoid treating a smooth posterior mean map as observed truth.
  • State when inference is interpolation versus extrapolation.

3. Space-time covariance

bayes_st_covariance() provides a dependency-light separable covariance utility for teaching, simulation, and design sensitivity studies.

d <- bayes_teaching_data("spatiotemporal")
des <- bayes_spatiotemporal(d, "yield", "x", "y", "day", ~ treatment, subject = "plot_id")
if (TRUE) bayes_st_monitor(des)

Interpretation checklist

  • Identify the experimental unit and the repeated series.
  • Keep treatment effects distinct from latent spatial and temporal structure.
  • Quantify uncertainty on the response scale.
  • Avoid treating a smooth posterior mean map as observed truth.
  • State when inference is interpolation versus extrapolation.

4. Temporal persistence

The validated first route uses AR(1) dependence within an explicit subject or series. Factor-time and linear-time alternatives are available for sensitivity analysis.

d <- bayes_teaching_data("spatiotemporal")
des <- bayes_spatiotemporal(d, "yield", "x", "y", "day", ~ treatment, subject = "plot_id")
if (FALSE) bayes_st_monitor(des)

Interpretation checklist

  • Identify the experimental unit and the repeated series.
  • Keep treatment effects distinct from latent spatial and temporal structure.
  • Quantify uncertainty on the response scale.
  • Avoid treating a smooth posterior mean map as observed truth.
  • State when inference is interpolation versus extrapolation.

5. Gaussian field

The spatial component is represented by a two-dimensional Gaussian process. Spatial scale and temporal persistence answer different scientific questions.

d <- bayes_teaching_data("spatiotemporal")
des <- bayes_spatiotemporal(d, "yield", "x", "y", "day", ~ treatment, subject = "plot_id")
if (FALSE) bayes_st_monitor(des)

Interpretation checklist

  • Identify the experimental unit and the repeated series.
  • Keep treatment effects distinct from latent spatial and temporal structure.
  • Quantify uncertainty on the response scale.
  • Avoid treating a smooth posterior mean map as observed truth.
  • State when inference is interpolation versus extrapolation.

6. Workflow

The standard workflow remains design, audit, plan, fit, diagnose, predict, and report. Version 1.2.0 does not create a parallel API.

d <- bayes_teaching_data("spatiotemporal")
des <- bayes_spatiotemporal(d, "yield", "x", "y", "day", ~ treatment, subject = "plot_id")
if (TRUE) bayes_st_monitor(des)

Interpretation checklist

  • Identify the experimental unit and the repeated series.
  • Keep treatment effects distinct from latent spatial and temporal structure.
  • Quantify uncertainty on the response scale.
  • Avoid treating a smooth posterior mean map as observed truth.
  • State when inference is interpolation versus extrapolation.

7. Monitoring coverage

bayes_st_monitor() reports locations, times, location-time coverage, duplicates, and series-level time coverage before model fitting.

d <- bayes_teaching_data("spatiotemporal")
des <- bayes_spatiotemporal(d, "yield", "x", "y", "day", ~ treatment, subject = "plot_id")
if (FALSE) bayes_st_monitor(des)

Interpretation checklist

  • Identify the experimental unit and the repeated series.
  • Keep treatment effects distinct from latent spatial and temporal structure.
  • Quantify uncertainty on the response scale.
  • Avoid treating a smooth posterior mean map as observed truth.
  • State when inference is interpolation versus extrapolation.

8. Posterior prediction

bayes_st_predict() delegates to the common posterior prediction engine while preserving the explicit space-time interpretation.

d <- bayes_teaching_data("spatiotemporal")
des <- bayes_spatiotemporal(d, "yield", "x", "y", "day", ~ treatment, subject = "plot_id")
if (FALSE) bayes_st_monitor(des)

Interpretation checklist

  • Identify the experimental unit and the repeated series.
  • Keep treatment effects distinct from latent spatial and temporal structure.
  • Quantify uncertainty on the response scale.
  • Avoid treating a smooth posterior mean map as observed truth.
  • State when inference is interpolation versus extrapolation.

9. Forecasting

bayes_st_forecast() requires future times unless interpolation is explicitly allowed. Forecasting outside the observed spatial or temporal domain must be interpreted cautiously.

d <- bayes_teaching_data("spatiotemporal")
des <- bayes_spatiotemporal(d, "yield", "x", "y", "day", ~ treatment, subject = "plot_id")
if (TRUE) bayes_st_monitor(des)

Interpretation checklist

  • Identify the experimental unit and the repeated series.
  • Keep treatment effects distinct from latent spatial and temporal structure.
  • Quantify uncertainty on the response scale.
  • Avoid treating a smooth posterior mean map as observed truth.
  • State when inference is interpolation versus extrapolation.

10. Exceedance probabilities

bayes_st_exceedance() converts posterior predictions to probabilities of exceeding or falling below a scientifically meaningful response threshold.

d <- bayes_teaching_data("spatiotemporal")
des <- bayes_spatiotemporal(d, "yield", "x", "y", "day", ~ treatment, subject = "plot_id")
if (FALSE) bayes_st_monitor(des)

Interpretation checklist

  • Identify the experimental unit and the repeated series.
  • Keep treatment effects distinct from latent spatial and temporal structure.
  • Quantify uncertainty on the response scale.
  • Avoid treating a smooth posterior mean map as observed truth.
  • State when inference is interpolation versus extrapolation.

11. Change probabilities

bayes_st_change() compares matched locations across two times draw by draw and returns posterior change intervals and probabilities.

d <- bayes_teaching_data("spatiotemporal")
des <- bayes_spatiotemporal(d, "yield", "x", "y", "day", ~ treatment, subject = "plot_id")
if (FALSE) bayes_st_monitor(des)

Interpretation checklist

  • Identify the experimental unit and the repeated series.
  • Keep treatment effects distinct from latent spatial and temporal structure.
  • Quantify uncertainty on the response scale.
  • Avoid treating a smooth posterior mean map as observed truth.
  • State when inference is interpolation versus extrapolation.

12. Diagnostics

Convergence, ESS, R-hat, posterior predictive checks, spatial process scales, temporal AR parameters, and residual structure should all be reported.

d <- bayes_teaching_data("spatiotemporal")
des <- bayes_spatiotemporal(d, "yield", "x", "y", "day", ~ treatment, subject = "plot_id")
if (TRUE) bayes_st_monitor(des)

Interpretation checklist

  • Identify the experimental unit and the repeated series.
  • Keep treatment effects distinct from latent spatial and temporal structure.
  • Quantify uncertainty on the response scale.
  • Avoid treating a smooth posterior mean map as observed truth.
  • State when inference is interpolation versus extrapolation.

13. Agronomic interpretation

Examples include soil moisture monitoring, disease progression, plant growth, repeated field maps, and multi-year trials.

d <- bayes_teaching_data("spatiotemporal")
des <- bayes_spatiotemporal(d, "yield", "x", "y", "day", ~ treatment, subject = "plot_id")
if (FALSE) bayes_st_monitor(des)

Interpretation checklist

  • Identify the experimental unit and the repeated series.
  • Keep treatment effects distinct from latent spatial and temporal structure.
  • Quantify uncertainty on the response scale.
  • Avoid treating a smooth posterior mean map as observed truth.
  • State when inference is interpolation versus extrapolation.

14. Limitations

The 1.2.0 validated route is a Gaussian-process plus AR(1) model. Fully nonseparable dynamic fields and SPDE engines remain future extensions rather than silently approximated features.

d <- bayes_teaching_data("spatiotemporal")
des <- bayes_spatiotemporal(d, "yield", "x", "y", "day", ~ treatment, subject = "plot_id")
if (FALSE) bayes_st_monitor(des)

Interpretation checklist

  • Identify the experimental unit and the repeated series.
  • Keep treatment effects distinct from latent spatial and temporal structure.
  • Quantify uncertainty on the response scale.
  • Avoid treating a smooth posterior mean map as observed truth.
  • State when inference is interpolation versus extrapolation.

15. Reproducibility

Record coordinate units, time units, kernel, temporal representation, priors, backend, seed, chains, diagnostics, prediction grid, and thresholds.

d <- bayes_teaching_data("spatiotemporal")
des <- bayes_spatiotemporal(d, "yield", "x", "y", "day", ~ treatment, subject = "plot_id")
if (TRUE) bayes_st_monitor(des)

Interpretation checklist

  • Identify the experimental unit and the repeated series.
  • Keep treatment effects distinct from latent spatial and temporal structure.
  • Quantify uncertainty on the response scale.
  • Avoid treating a smooth posterior mean map as observed truth.
  • State when inference is interpolation versus extrapolation.

Integrated example 

d <- bayes_teaching_data("spatiotemporal")
des <- bayes_spatiotemporal(d, "yield", "x", "y", "day", ~ treatment, subject = "plot_id", spatial_cov = "matern32")
audit <- bayes_design_audit(des)
plan <- bayes_plan(des)
mon <- bayes_st_monitor(des)
S <- bayes_st_covariance(des, spatial_range = 2, temporal_rho = 0.7, nugget = 0.15)
# fit <- bayes_fit(des, engine = "brms")
# bayes_st_parameters(fit)
# bayes_st_predict(fit)
# bayes_st_exceedance(fit, threshold = 6)

Reporting template

Report the scientific design, coordinate reference/units, time scale, number of locations and times, temporal series definition, spatial covariance kernel, temporal dependence, priors, computation settings, convergence diagnostics, posterior predictive checks, process-parameter summaries, fixed agronomic effects, prediction uncertainty, and any exceedance or change threshold.
